Innate factors and ontogeny determine nonbreeding areas of migrant songbirds

Axes labels
x - Longitude
y - Latitude

Line colours show the locations of the breeding populations.

Orange - Spain
Purple - Norway
Blue - Sweden
Pink - Britain
Red - Netherlands
Turquoise - western Russia
Green - Ural
Dark green - Siberia

Shapes show the type of site:

Circles - breeding site
Squares - non-breeding area (this is the winter location)
Filled upward triangles - autumn post-Saharan stopover location
Filled downward triangles - spring Iberian stopover location
Open downward triangles - spring westernmost location

```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
library(maps)
```


Pipe symbol
```{r}
my_numbers <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)

sum(my_numbers)
```
```{r}
#Pipe passes the value on its left into the function on its right
my_numbers <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)

my_numbers |> sum()

my_numbers <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)

print(my_numbers |>
  sum() |>
  sqrt())
```
```{r}
#Steps can be added indefinitely
my_numbers <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)

print(my_numbers |>
  sum() |>
  sqrt() |>
  round())
```
```{r}
my_numbers <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)

my_result <- my_numbers |>
  sum() |>
  sqrt() |>
  round()

print(my_result)
```
```{r}
input_vec <- c(5, -10, 4, -3)

result <- input_vec |>
  mean()|>
  abs() |>
  round() 
  
  print(result)

```
Comparison operators
```{r}
#== means "is equal to?"
x <- 1
round(3.123, digits = 1)
x <- 1
y <- 2
print(x == y)
```
```{r}
y <- 12
print (y == 7)
print (y <15)
print (y>20)
print (y<=12)

```
Joining data frame
```{r}
df_dept <- read_csv("data/depts.csv")
df_score <- read_csv("data/scores.csv")
gt(df_dept)
gt(df_score)
```

```{r}
#full join retains all of the rows from both data frames, adding NA where no data is available
full_join_example <- full_join(df_dept, df_score)
gt(full_join_example)

```

```{r}
#inner join only retains rows for individuals which are in both data frame
inner_join_example <- inner_join(df_dept, df_score)
gt(inner_join_example)
```
```{r}
#left join retains all rows in the first data frame  and adds data from the second data frame where available, adding NA where it is not.
left_join_example <- left_join(df_dept, df_score)
gt(left_join_example)
```
```{r}
#right join retains all the rows in the second data frame and adds data from the first data frame where available, adding NA where it is not.
right_join_example <- right_join(df_dept, df_score)
gt(right_join_example)
```
```{r}
gt(df_dept)
```
```{r}
#subsetting data frame. Filter allows to filter data out based from a specific column, %in% allows filtering from multiple values
keep_depts <- c("Maths", "English")

df_eng_maths <- df_dept |>
  filter(Department %in% keep_depts)

gt(df_eng_maths)
```
